dedupe_keys.name: tree d fusion 600 000 simulation ready 3d urban tree models for north america

description: Tree-D Fusion is a collection of 600,000 simulation-ready 3D models of real urban trees across North America, each reconstructed from a street view image in Google's Auto Arborist dataset with its genus label. Jae Joong Lee, Bosheng Li, Sara Beery, Jonathan Huang, Songlin Fei, Raymond Yeh and Bedrich Benes of Purdue, MIT and Google presented it at ECCV 2024, with USDA support. The method uses two tree-adapted diffusion models guided by genus prompts to reconstruct a 3D crown envelope filled with markers, then grows a branching structure with a space colonisation algorithm, so the models can be run in tree growth and environment simulations. Coverage is trees in North American cities covered by Auto Arborist. Format and access: model files in a public Google Drive folder, code on GitHub and the paper on arXiv. Licence: not stated for the data; the paper is CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: shapes are inferred from single images, so hidden parts are generated, not measured. It supports urban forest digital twins for heat, storm-damage and line-clearance studies. Related catalogue records are Treepedia's Green View Index and the 5 million city trees dataset.
